changes.before: The Committee anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate in order to attain a stance of monetary policy that is sufficiently restrictive to return inflation to 2 percent over time.
changes.after: The Committee anticipates that some additional policy firming may be appropriate in order to attain a stance of monetary policy that is sufficiently restrictive to return inflation to 2 percent over time.
Recent developments are likely to result in tighter credit conditions for households and businesses and to weigh on economic activity, hiring, and inflation. The extent of these effects is uncertain.
The Committee will closely monitor incoming information and assess the implications for monetary policy.

changes.before: Inflation has eased somewhat but remains elevated.
Job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.
changes.after: Job gains have picked up in recent months and are running at a robust pace; the unemployment rate has remained low.
The U.S. banking system is sound and resilient.

changes.before: The Committee is highly attentive to inflation risks.
changes.after: The Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks.

parsed.rationale: Although rates were raised another 25bp and inflation/labor descriptions firmed, the forward guidance softened from "ongoing increases" to "some additional policy firming may be appropriate", signaling a nearing end to hikes. New language on tighter credit conditions weighing on activity and inflation adds a further dovish tilt.

spans.quote: The Committee anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate in order to attain a stance of monetary policy that is sufficiently restrictive to return inflation to 2 percent over time.
Inflation has eased somewhat but remains elevated.
Job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.
The Committee is highly attentive to inflation risks.

The Committee anticipates that some additional policy firming may be appropriate in order to attain a stance of monetary policy that is sufficiently restrictive to return inflation to 2 percent over time.
Recent developments are likely to result in tighter credit conditions for households and businesses and to weigh on economic activity, hiring, and inflation. The extent of these effects is uncertain.
The Committee will closely monitor incoming information and assess the implications for monetary policy.
Job gains have picked up in recent months and are running at a robust pace; the unemployment rate has remained low.
The U.S. banking system is sound and resilient.
The Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks.
